resume: Submitting a social housing application in Réunion, getting your unique number, gathering the right documents (including those related to a separation) and renewing the application on time.
aQuoiCaSert: Social housing has a regulated rent and is allocated subject to income limits. The application, online or at a registration office, gives you a unique number (numéro unique), which starts the clock on how long your application has been waiting. After a separation, you can have only your own income taken into account, provided you supply the right supporting documents.
quiEstConcerne: Households whose income does not exceed the limits set for the overseas territories.
Parents who are separating and need to find new housing with their children.
Foreign nationals holding a valid residence permit or receipt (récépissé).
aSavoir: Income limits in the overseas territories, including Réunion, for an application made in 2026 (2024 income, general case): €27,382 for 1 person, €36,567 for 2, €43,973 for 3, €53,088 for 4. They apply to the total income of all the people to be housed.
Single parent: with 1 dependent, the limit used is the one for 3 people (€43,973); with 2 dependents, the one for 4 people (€53,088).

Separation: to have only your income taken into account, attach proof such as the document referring the case to the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF), the divorce judgment or the birth certificate noting the dissolution of the PACS (civil partnership).
Everyone to be housed must be declared, including children in shared residence.

Renewal: an application that has not been met must be renewed every year. According to service-public.gouv.fr, it must be renewed within 11 months of its registration; without renewal, it is cancelled and you lose the time your application has been waiting.
Update the application as soon as your situation changes (separation, birth, new address, drop in income).

Valid ID document or residence permit for each adult, everyone's 2025 tax notice, proof of separation and judgment on the children's residence if you are separated, family record book.
